method: The QA profile's interop assemblies are IL2CPP proxies: every method body is an il2cpp_runtime_invoke of a token, so a member's existence, signature, field offset and enum values are readable metadata, while a body, a call order and a refusal path are not. Every claim below is a signature-level claim, and everything the game would have to confirm is listed under `unverified`.

sources.note: the decompiled interop assemblies this slice read; PlayerAgent.cs, PlayerSync.cs, Dam_PlayerDamageBase.cs, Dam_PlayerDamageLocal.cs, AgentModifierManager.cs, AgentModifier.cs, PlayerLocomotion.cs, PlayerSpawnpoint.cs, pInfection.cs, pInfectionMode.cs, pInfectionEffect.cs, pPlayerWarp.cs, pPlayerControlsToggle.cs, eDimensionIndex.cs

readbacks.use: the host entry this action submits; the session half of the same request is PlayerSync.SendSyncWarp
the packet send the warp request ends in
the receive half every other machine runs, so one host request is what a client sees
the packet the pair above shares; pPlayerWarp carries DimensionIndex, Position, LookDir and Options
the game's own landing solver; a false answer refuses the command with `destination-unavailable`
the states a warp is accepted in; a state outside the set is refused with `warp-state-refused` before anything is submitted
the action submits `None`: an authored teleport moves one life and plays no warp presentation
the action teleports in `Reality`, the dimension the level geometry a `vector3` destination names lives in
the readback that decides the commit: a position outside the tolerance is `warp-not-observed`, never a success
the value the row reports: read before the write, re-read for the preflight proof, and read again after it
the one replicated write entry this action submits: mode `Set` or `Add`, the sync flag set, and the page map refreshed
the local player's override of the same virtual entry; the action calls the base signature and the runtime dispatches
the private receive half, reached through SNet_Packet<pInfection> m_receiveModifyInfectionPacket; this is why the entry above is a replicated write and not a local field write

readbacks.signature: struct pInfection { System.Single amount @0; pInfectionMode mode @4; pInfectionEffect effect @5 }
readbacks.use: the one value the write carries; it has no source field, so the catalog's `source` entity is validated and never invented into the value
`add` is submitted as the native addition; `set` and `subtract` are submitted as absolute values because there is no subtract mode
the action submits `None`: the catalog row changes infection, it does not disinfect
read as evidence that infection is a modelled value with thresholds; the action does not read them and does not treat any of them as a ceiling
not consulted: whether immunity suppresses this write is not readable from metadata, so an immune receiver shows up as a readback that does not match and is reported as an unknown commit

facts.claim: One host call to `PlayerAgent.RequestWarpToSync` is the game's own warp request and its replication path: `PlayerSync.SendSyncWarp` sends `pPlayerWarp` on `m_warpPacket` and `PlayerSync.IncomingSyncWarp` receives it on every other machine.
facts.basis: the three members live in one build with the packet field between them; `IncomingSyncWarp` is the only receiver of that packet type
facts.inference: the call order and whether the host applies the warp locally before or after the send are not readable from metadata

facts.claim: `RequestWarpToSync` returns void, so a refusal on the game's side is not an answer this action can read.
facts.basis: the signature; the value-returning entry of the same family is `TryWarpTo` (System.Boolean), which is not the sync path
facts.consequence: the action proves the effect instead: the agent's own position after the call is what a row reports

facts.claim: `SampleWarpPosition` is the game's own landing solver for a dimension and a reference position.
facts.basis: a static entry taking the dimension, a reference position and an out result; the action treats a false answer as `destination-unavailable` rather than warping to an unvalidated coordinate

facts.claim: `m_warpableStates` holds the locomotion states the agent accepts a warp in, and the action's preflight is the same membership test.
facts.basis: a HashSet<PLOC_State> on the agent, next to the warp entries; the action refuses a state outside it by name

facts.claim: `ModifyInfection(data, sync, updatePageMap)` is the replicated infection write: the receiver's own `ReceiveModifyInfection` is private and reached through `m_receiveModifyInfectionPacket`, so a caller outside the class has this entry only.
facts.basis: the private receive member and the packet field; the local player's override of the same virtual entry confirms it is the game's own path and not a Forge-side field write
facts.inference: the meaning of the third parameter is taken from its name: `true` keeps the receiver's page-map state as current as a vanilla change leaves it

facts.claim: The native value has no subtraction mode, so a `subtract` operation is computed as an absolute value by this action.
facts.basis: pInfectionMode has exactly Set and Add

facts.claim: The value the row reports is the receiver's own readback, never the requested amount.
facts.basis: the Infection field is read after the write; a value that does not match what the operation asked for is an unknown commit

notImplemented.reason: No native request path exists. The catalog row asks for a new life, and nothing in this build allocates one: `PlayerAgent.Alive` is a virtual property with a setter (token 100681779) that writes a flag, not a life; `PlayerSpawnpoint` only positions an existing spawn (`SetPoint` 100682775, `SetSeat` 100682776, `SetStartState` 100682780, `EnableAtPoint` 100682781, fields m_point/m_hasPoint/m_seat/m_startState); `PlayerAgent.TryWarpBack` (token 100681847) returns to a recorded position; and no `Respawn` member exists on PlayerAgent, PlayerManager, PlayerSpawnpoint or any replication type in the decompiled tree.
notImplemented.consequence: no binding is registered, so an export that pins the row is refused by the release manifest rather than half-working in game
notImplemented.wouldNeed: a native spawn/request entry (or the replication path's own spawn request) plus the inventory restore the row's second policy names

notImplemented.reason: The native entry cannot carry the declared shape. The only control gate is a single boolean for every control: `PlayerAgent.RequestToggleControlsEnabled(System.Boolean)` (token 100681844), replicated by `PlayerSync.SendToggleControlsEnabled(System.Boolean)` (token 100682852) over `m_controlsTogglePacket` and `pPlayerControlsToggle{ Value }`. The catalog's `action` parameter is the `equipment_action` set (primary, secondary, reload, interact, recall, alternate, custom-binding) with a tick duration, a reason and an `effect` handle output — per-action gating, an expiry and a handle none of which that entry has.
notImplemented.reshape: replace the per-action set with the native boolean gate and drop the duration/handle, the same conclusion the weapon group's `action_lock` reached; the row's evidence is this entry, not a per-action table
notImplemented.wouldNeed: either a per-action native gate or the row's shape changed to what the gate really is

notImplemented.reason: Its `snapshot` input is a `transaction` handle, and the transaction/reservation store is a framework capability this build does not have; on the native side there is no inventory restore to call either. `PlayerSync.SyncInventory(System.Boolean,SNet_Player)` (token 100682856) pushes the inventory a player holds right now, which is a different operation from restoring a captured one; `TryCollectCaptureData` exists on placed things (BarrierInstance, iSentrygunInstance_Sync, MapperDronePlaced) over `pItemSpawnData`/`pGearSpawnData`, not over the player's inventory.
notImplemented.consequence: the row stays unregistered; the capture half (checkpoint_save/restore) is another slice's row, and registering the restore half without a snapshot to consume would be a plan that cannot load

unverified.question: Does the host apply the warp synchronously inside RequestWarpToSync, so an immediate position readback already shows the landing point?
unverified.why: no body was decompiled and no game run happened; a warp that lands a frame later would make this action report `warp-not-observed` for a warp that did happen
unverified.handling: the action reports the truth it can read: the agent's position after the call. If the game is asynchronous, the tolerance check has to move to a later read (a follow-up read needs cross-dispatch state the runtime holds)

unverified.question: Is `eDimensionIndex.Reality` always the dimension a level coordinate belongs to?
unverified.why: the catalog's row carries no dimension port and no evidence names one; `Reality` is the only member a level position can mean
unverified.handling: the choice is one constant in `PlayerActions`; a row that gains a dimension port replaces it

unverified.question: How far from the solved landing point can a completed warp leave the agent?
unverified.why: the native path may resolve colliders or offset the position; 0.5 m is this action's own threshold, not a native constant
unverified.handling: documented as the action's threshold; a game run should measure it

unverified.question: What range does `Dam_PlayerDamageBase.Infection` hold (0..1? percent?), and does the native write clamp it or apply resistance?
unverified.why: metadata gives the field and the mode only; the catalog's design notes call the unit a percentage while the port declares no unit
unverified.handling: the action passes the amount through unchanged and reports the readback: a receiver that stores a different value is an unknown commit. No conversion and no assumed ceiling

unverified.question: What does the third parameter of `ModifyInfection` do?
unverified.handling: the action passes true, the value a change that must leave the receiver's own state current would take; a game run should confirm

unverified.question: Does `ToggleInfectionImmunity` suppress this write path?
unverified.why: the property exists but its effect on ModifyInfection is not readable from metadata
unverified.handling: not consulted: an immune receiver is reported as a readback that did not match (unknown commit) rather than being pre-refused on a guess

unverified.question: That a client actually observes the warp and the infection change of the host's commands.
unverified.why: no two-machine run happened; the claim rests on the packet pairs being the game's own replication path
unverified.handling: listed as a game-verified item for the acceptance run

limits: No native invocation, no game execution and no multiplayer run happened for this slice
Harmony hook points, virtual dispatch and native call order are not resolved by this evidence; the two actions call the game's own entries rather than hooking anything
The interop signatures are read from the frozen Forge-MapEditor-QA profile copy named above
